messages:
Anya: Heads-up — after the last onboarding run we had a couple of odd fallthroughs where prober signals disagreed with bench verdicts. thinking we need a short triage and a more explicit fallback contract for the prober->admit boundary.
Michael: +1. can you paste an example of the disagreement?
Anya: Here — model xg-7-small: bench says PASS (latency & quality within thresholds) but prober returned WARN because it hit a kv-cache mismatch on replay. Bench run: 2024-11-08 21:13, Prober log snippet: `kv replay mismatch: key len 0 vs expected 16`
Sanjay: Hmm. That kv mismatch is noisy for newer quantized binaries. Our prober currently treats any mismatch as WARN which causes canary traffic to get clipped. maybe we need a severity enum.
Lina: Agree — we should codify severity and an action map. e.g. FAIL => block admission; WARN => allow admission but route to slowpath & escalate; INFO => attach to telemetry only. Would reduce false blocked models.
Anya: I sketched a minimal contract for the signal envelope: ```proto
message AdmitSignal {
  string model_id = 1;
  enum Severity { INFO = 0; WARN = 1; FAIL = 2; }
  Severity severity = 2;
  repeated string tags = 3;
  string note = 4;
}
```
Michael: Looks reasonable. tradeoff: transforms like this push decision logic to prober authors or to admitting service. where do we want the policy to live?
Sanjay: My vote is to keep prober lightweight: emit severity hints + reasons, but policy maps live in the admit service. That way infra teams can change action without republishing prober code.
Lina: Policy-on-admit also lets us A/B different actions per org. But downside: admit service needs to understand reason taxonomy and remain backwards compatible.
Anya: Right. operationally we saw that changing the prober (fixing the kv-mismatch noise) took 3 days and blocked several teams. If admit had a default policy that treated kv-mismatch as INFO for quantized models, we could have avoided the blockage.
Michael: What about cost? If we make admit decision heavier (fetching golden inputs, running a quick cohort replay), latency and cost per admission increase. We need SLOs for the admit API.
Sanjay: Suggest split: light admit path (fast decision, uses severity mapping) and a post-admit verification job that runs deeper checks async and can trigger rollbacks. Keep admission synchronous < 500ms for UX.
Lina: Implementation sketch: 1) prober emits AdmitSignal stream to kafka topic `admit.signals.v2` 2) admit service consumes, applies policy (config-driven), responds to intake API 3) async verifier job kicks off heavier bench runs if severity >= WARN 4) results feed back into policy dashboard
Anya: That would let Dedicated/Private customers override policy via config and still get the same prober behavior. matches our product thesis.
Michael: How do we version the signal schema? we need forward/back compat. propose `version` field and `tags` for unknown reasons.
Sanjay: Yes — version + optional freeform `details` blob (json string) for future experiments. but keep core enums stable.
Anya: Another open thing: what signals do we include? currently prober emits {latency, throughput, kv_consistency, output_equivalence, compile_errors}. Do we add `golden_coverage`?
Lina: Add golden_coverage but as INFO by default. If coverage < X% and severity WARN, route to canary-only deploy.
Michael: Also want a mechanism to silence known noisy checks (e.g., specific quantized backends). maybe per-model annotations in registry: `admit_overrides: {kv_mismatch: INFO}`
Sanjay: Registry overrides are preferable to baking exceptions into prober. admit service should consult registry annotations at decision time.
Anya: Ok plan: short RFC follow-up tasks — 1) formalize AdmitSignal proto + version (Anya) 2) prototype admit-side policy engine with config file and registry lookup (Michael) 3) async verifier job spec + dashboard hooks (Lina) 4) BenchBot: add golden_coverage metric to prober payload (BenchBot)
BenchBot: noted — will emit `golden_coverage` in next deploy, sample rate 1/5 for cost control. :robot_face: 
Lina: timeline? aim for lightweight policy engine + proto v1 in 2 weeks so we can unblock ongoing model admissions.
Michael: I'll take the engine prototype. will mock registry responses initially.
Sanjay: I'll do the spec for async verifier and rollback hooks.
Anya: Thanks — I'll post the proto draft in the RFC channel and link it here. We'll iterate on the taxonomy. :thumbsup:
